Security advisory: Critical remote code execution vulnerabilities, update now

Security advisory: Critical remote code execution vulnerabilities, update now

AI 作者 xd 热度 1543 回复 656 2026/10/21 04:15
打开原帖 打开外部链接 JSON

摘要

  • Here are the most important news items we have published in 2026 on PHP.net.
  • 23 Oct 2026 Informational advisory: Session upload progress We suggest you set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next regular bugfix release, to fully protect from an unlikely RCE vector. This setting was already listed as a mitigation in the GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp advisory for CVE-2026-109619 published on Oct 21st, 2026. If you applied it then, keep it in place and no further action is needed. The issue can only occur under an unusual combination of configuration and application code. An application must set session.serialize_handler to php_binary or php_serialize in its configuration and then switch it to php at runtime with ini_set() before calling session_start(). Session upload progress must also still be enabled. Applications that never change the serialize handler at runtime can keep the feature enabled. Since this setup is unlikely in practice, we are handling it in the regular release cycle and will publish a full advisory for CVE-2026-115560 with the next release.

TekMol 2026/10/21 16:59
Many here call for an earlier release of the patch.

But it is not clear if releasing the fix early would make the damage smaller or larger.

Having the patch probably makes creating an exploit easier. So the number of attacks would increase.

There is no way to coordinate the whole world on an earlier time. I would guess the number of people who have to patch their instances is in the hundreds of thousands.

Everybody who actively watches the topic already has the option to shut down their instances.

So ringing the bell and getting as many people as possible to shut down their webservers now and patch at 14:00 might be the best in terms of damage minimisation.

By the way, it is not enough to just "shutdown -h now" and then later restart and "apt update && apt upgrade". The moment the machine comes back, it can get hacked. So you should make sure the webserver does not start after the next boot. For Apache this would be something like "rm /etc/systemd/system/multi-user.target.wants/apache2.service" and then after patching recreate the symlink via something like "ln -s /lib/systemd/system/apache2.service /etc/systemd/system/multi-user.target.wants/apache2.service".
